title.en: Calculus and Optimisation for Machine Learning
title.ar: التفاضل والتكامل والأمثلة الرياضية لتعلم الآلة

tagline: REPLACE: one line under the title: what participants can do after the course
description: Participants work through the calculus that trains models: derivatives as local linear approximations, gradients, Jacobians and the chain rule on computational graphs. They backpropagate by hand, then write a small reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine and check it against a framework. They run batch, stochastic and momentum gradient descent, read loss curves, and handle convexity and constraints. The capstone trains a small network with their own engine; tensor-level differentiation and modern optimisers follow in SPC-DLR-302.
audience: Beginners. Career changers and non-computing graduates closing bridging gaps before advanced study, and computing graduates refreshing the mathematics behind models; a placement test lets participants skip any course whose content they already command.
prerequisites: FND-MTH-101 Linear Algebra for Machine Learning
School calculus: derivatives of polynomials and exponentials, or the pre-work refresher
Writes short Python programs with functions and loops (FND-PRG-101 or equivalent)

outcomes.text: Explain derivatives, partial derivatives, gradients and Jacobians as local linear approximations, given functions of one and several variables
outcomes.evidence: supervised AI-off test, at least 70% correct

outcomes.text: Distinguish convex from non-convex objectives and describe how saddle points and step size shape gradient descent, given six loss surfaces with optimisation traces
outcomes.evidence: annotated plots marked against a reference

outcomes.text: Explain how a constraint moves the optimum of a small problem, using the Lagrangian and the meaning of its multiplier, given three problems, including a budget allocation
outcomes.evidence: written solutions marked against a rubric, with each multiplier read as the price of the constraint

outcomes.text: Compute gradients of a composite function by applying the chain rule backwards through a computational graph, given a two-example logistic-regression loss
outcomes.evidence: a hand-worked backward pass matching a numerical gradient check

outcomes.text: Implement reverse-mode automatic differentiation for scalar operations and verify it with finite-difference checks, given a starter interface and test suite
outcomes.evidence: an engine that passes the tests and agrees with a framework's gradients

outcomes.text: Apply batch, stochastic and momentum gradient descent and diagnose divergence or slow convergence from loss curves, given losses on public data
outcomes.evidence: an experiment log with learning-rate sweeps and a diagnosis of each failed run
